question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing home care notes?

options.A: Brief and casual phrases to save time
options.B: Objective, specific, and measurable details
options.C: General summaries and personal opinions
options.D: Emotional descriptions of the family dynamic

explanation: You got it! Stick to clear, factual observations so any other nurse reading your notes knows the exact status of the patient.

question: What is the tongue's main job right at the start of swallowing food?

options.A: Producing digestive enzymes to break down starches
options.B: Sealing off the nasopharynx to prevent nasal regurgitation
options.C: Pushing the food bolus backward against the hard palate
options.D: Opening the upper esophageal sphincter mechanically

explanation: When you swallow, your tongue acts like a natural spatula, pressing food up and back toward your throat.

question: What does 'statistical power' mean in a research study?

options.A: The physical strength required by nurses to lift heavy patients
options.B: The total amount of funding secured for laboratory equipment
options.C: The ability of the study to detect a true effect if one exists
options.D: The speed at which data is entered into a computer spreadsheet

explanation: You got it! Power is basically your study's muscle—its ability to catch a real treatment difference if it's actually there.

question: What happens to perishable foods when transport infrastructure is poor?

options.A: They last much longer without refrigeration.
options.B: They spoil before reaching the market.
options.C: They become much cheaper to buy for villagers.
options.D: They turn into dry grains automatically.

explanation: Without good roads and cold storage transport, fresh foods easily rot before they can make the long journey to market.

question: What is the traditional foundation for caring for the sick and elderly in Nigerian society?

options.A: Missionary parish health outposts
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: State-run geriatric nursing homes
options.D: Private commercial health agencies

explanation: In our culture, we lean heavily on extended family members to look after and support older or sick relatives at home. Beautiful tradition!

question: Which type of injury happens primarily from breathing in superheated air and smoke?

options.A: Surgical disruption
options.B: Inhalational injury
options.C: Blunt neck trauma
options.D: Penetrating trauma

explanation: Well done! Heat and toxic chemicals from smoke directly burn and damage the delicate lining of the upper airway.

question: Why are portable monitors so great for catching sudden changes in a patient's condition?

options.A: They provide continuous, real-time physiological data outside the bedside
options.B: They eliminate the need for any manual vital sign documentation
options.C: They completely prevent the occurrence of false alarms
options.D: They automatically diagnose underlying diseases without nurse input

explanation: Because they track vitals continuously—even during transport—we can spot sudden warning signs immediately and act fast.

question: What is a major challenge that family caregivers often face when looking after a sick relative at home?

options.A: Burnout and physical exhaustion
options.B: Over-staffing by professional nurses
options.C: Excessive financial compensation
options.D: Too much free time and boredom

explanation: Exactly right. Caregiver fatigue is real! Looking after a loved one without a break can easily lead to physical and emotional burnout.

question: Why is 'closed-loop communication' so important during a chaotic resuscitation?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from having to touch the patient
options.B: It confirms that instructions given by the team leader are clearly heard and executed
options.C: It ensures that family members outside the room stay quiet
options.D: It reduces the need for documentation after the code is over

explanation: Brilliant! Repeating instructions back (like 'Giving 1mg epinephrine now') stops dangerous mistakes when things get loud and fast.

question: Which part of the chain of infection do standard precautions target the most?

options.A: The mode of transmission
options.B: The susceptible host
options.C: The microbial reservoir
options.D: The infectious agent itself

explanation: You got it! Barriers like gloves, masks, and hand hygiene cut off the travel route, stopping pathogens from moving from the source to the patient or nurse.

question: What is the main job of a midwifery kit in community health work?

options.A: To provide tools and meds for childbirth care and quick emergency help
options.B: To serve as a mini operating room for a big city hospital
options.C: To store personal items for community health workers during long trips
options.D: To collect lab samples for community malaria screening

explanation: Think of the midwifery kit as a birth attendant's best friend in the field—it packs all the essential tools and meds needed to safely manage deliveries at the primary healthcare level!

question: Why do our hands and lips take up so much more space in the brain's sensory map than our back?

options.A: They have thicker layers of subcutaneous fat
options.B: They are located closer to the brain
options.C: They receive a larger volume of arterial blood
options.D: They possess a much higher density of touch receptors

explanation: Makes sense, right? We use our hands and lips for detailed tasks, so they need way more brain power and receptor coverage than our backs!

question: Which of these is true about human resilience?

options.A: It only exists in professional athletes
options.B: It can be cultivated and developed over time
options.C: It disappears entirely after childhood
options.D: It is completely fixed at the time of birth

explanation: Resilience isn't something you're just born with. Like a muscle, it grows stronger with practice, good support, and coping skills.

question: What happens when health workers make promises to a community and fail to keep them?

options.A: Local leaders take over nursing duties
options.B: The community becomes more eager to help
options.C: Government funding increases automatically
options.D: Trust is broken, leading to poor cooperation

explanation: Broken promises destroy trust, making future health initiatives extremely difficult to implement. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why do scolding or confrontational approaches usually fail when counseling patients about drinking?

options.A: They cause the liver to metabolize alcohol at an unsafe, accelerated speed
options.B: They instantly cure the physiological addiction without patient consent
options.C: They make patients defensive and less likely to share honest information
options.D: They violate federal privacy laws regarding nutritional counseling

explanation: Nobody likes being judged! If a nurse is harsh, the patient will just shut down, hide their habits, and miss out on real help.

question: When picking a research design, what should be your number one guide?

options.A: The specific nature of the research question
options.B: The availability of colorful presentation software
options.C: The length of the reference list in textbooks
options.D: The personal preference of the hospital director

explanation: Correct! Always let your research question drive the bus—it tells you what kind of answer you need, which points straight to the right design.

question: How are resident skin germs different from the transient germs you pick up on the ward?

options.A: Transient flora permanently live inside the deeper layers of skin tissue
options.B: Transient flora cannot be washed off with regular soap and water
options.C: Resident flora live deep in the skin and are harder to remove completely
options.D: Resident flora are always deadly pathogens that cause quick disease

explanation: Resident flora are like permanent residents tucked deep in your skin crevices, while transient flora just sit loosely on top.

question: A nurse manager says, 'We must sterilize the surgical instruments every morning at 7 AM.' What kind of activity is this?

options.A: An objective
options.B: A mission
options.C: A goal
options.D: A task

explanation: Spot on! Doing a specific duty at a set time is a daily task that keeps the clinic running smoothly.

question: What is a core day-to-day nursing duty when it comes to reproductive health care?

options.A: Passing national laws regarding reproductive rights
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgical operations independently
options.C: Providing family planning counseling and education
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptives for hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Nurses spend a lot of time guiding clients through family planning choices and teaching healthy habits.

question: Which question addresses how a nursing team will track their progress during a quality project?

options.A: What are we trying to accomplish?
options.B: How will we know that a change is an improvement?
options.C: Who is responsible for the nursing budget?
options.D: What change can we make that will result in an improvement?

explanation: Well done! This question pushes the team to choose clear signs and measures to prove if their new ideas are actually working.

question: Why would a nurse check out a patient's home environment before they are discharged?

options.A: To identify physical barriers and fall hazards before discharge
options.B: To determine the financial income of the household members
options.C: To verify if the client owns a television or radio
options.D: To inspect the structural plumbing and electrical wiring

explanation: Safety first! Spotting dangerous things like loose rugs or stairs beforehand helps prevent nasty falls when they finally get home.

question: Which part of the limbic system looks like a seahorse and helps with memory?

options.A: The hippocampus
options.B: The amygdala
options.C: The hypothalamus
options.D: The fornix

explanation: You got it! The hippocampus has a distinct seahorse shape and is essential for helping you form and process new memories.

question: A nurse wants to make sure new health posters are clear before printing thousands of copies. What should she do?

options.A: Ask doctors in the capital city to review the picture quality
options.B: Distribute all the posters immediately to save transport costs
options.C: Pre-test the posters with a small group of local community members
options.D: Translate the medical text into Latin for a more professional look

explanation: Brilliant! Always pre-test your materials with the target audience first to catch confusing pictures or messages before mass printing.

question: What is the best way to stop a nasogastric tube from getting blocked?

options.A: Changing the tube to a smaller size every week
options.B: Adding cooking oil to every feed
options.C: Flushing it with warm water before and after feeds and drugs
options.D: Blowing air down the tube twice a shift

explanation: Regular water flushes wash away sticky food and medicine residue before they can dry up and clog your tube.

question: What is the most important first step when treating a baby with acute diarrhea?

options.A: Preventing dehydration using oral rehydration salts
options.B: Placing the infant on strict intravenous nutrition
options.C: Administering strong anti-diarrheal syrups
options.D: Stopping all forms of breastfeeding immediately

explanation: You got it! Giving oral rehydration salts (ORS) replaces lost water and salts, saving the baby from dangerous dehydration.

question: Why are all the steps in the chain of survival equally important?

options.A: Advanced drugs cannot be given before every step is completed
options.B: Each step must be performed by the exact same healthcare provider
options.C: Defibrillation will fail if the patient is not in a hospital bed
options.D: A failure in any single step drastically lowers overall survival odds

explanation: Think of it like a real chain—if one link breaks, the whole thing fails! Every single step helps give the patient the best fighting chance.

question: Why do raw spreadsheets often fail to convince hospital staff to change their practices?

options.A: Computer systems in hospitals block access to raw data files
options.B: Spreadsheets only contain financial data instead of clinical metrics
options.C: Nurses are legally not allowed to look at hospital spreadsheets
options.D: They lack the human context and emotional connection of a story

explanation: Spot on! Numbers alone don't show the real human struggles behind them, making it hard for busy nurses to connect with the data.

question: Which of the following is an example of a social determinant of health?

options.A: The personal willpower of an individual to avoid sickness
options.B: Access to safe drinking water and sanitation
options.C: The specific genetic blood type of a patient
options.D: The brand of medication prescribed by a doctor

explanation: Social determinants are external environmental, economic, and social conditions that powerfully influence whether people stay healthy or fall ill. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is community education just as important as passing laws to stop FGM?

options.A: It allows communities to vote on whether they want to follow federal laws
options.B: It addresses the root cultural beliefs and social norms that sustain the practice
options.C: It ensures that traditional cutters can find alternative paying jobs easily
options.D: It replaces the need for police officers and court systems entirely

explanation: Well done! Laws alone cannot change deeply held mindsets. Education helps communities willingly choose to leave the practice behind.

question: What is a common error when interpreting results from a descriptive study?

options.A: Using percentages to explain how many participants answered a survey
options.B: Concluding that one variable caused another simply because they occurred together
options.C: Creating a bar chart to display age groups in the sample
options.D: Comparing current findings with past published nursing literature

explanation: Just because two things happen at the same time doesn't mean one caused the other! Descriptive studies show connections, not direct causes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: When should you close, seal, and replace a sharps container?

options.A: Only when it is completely overflowing to save space
options.B: Whenever the outside gets a bit dusty
options.C: When it is about three-quarters full
options.D: At the very end of every month, no matter what

explanation: Safety first! Stopping at three-quarters full prevents people from trying to force more items in and accidentally getting a needle-stick injury.

question: A patient from a local community frequently visits the clinic complaining of severe body aches and fatigue, but medical tests find no physical cause. What should the nurse consider?

options.A: Physical complaints can never be linked to psychological stress
options.B: The patient is definitely fabricating symptoms to get prescription drugs
options.C: The laboratory equipment is likely malfunctioning and needs calibration
options.D: The patient might be expressing emotional distress through physical symptoms

explanation: Many individuals culturally communicate psychological distress through physical symptoms, requiring nurses to look beyond pure medical lab results. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why must nurse administrators think of themselves as trustees of the public trust?

options.A: Because public hospitals are funded by taxpayers and government money
options.B: Because patients pay private fees directly to the nurse manager
options.C: Because nurses legally own all hospital equipment and supplies
options.D: Because administrators are exempt from standard hospital rules

explanation: Think of it this way: since public hospitals run on money from everyday citizens and the government, we owe it to them to protect and use those resources wisely!

question: A community nurse notices that pregnant women in a remote village have nowhere to go for antenatal care. What is the best action?

options.A: Tell the pregnant women to relocate permanently to the capital
options.B: Ignore the issue since hospitals are solely a government duty
options.C: Collaborate with a voluntary health agency to set up mobile clinics
options.D: Wait until the villagers independently build a standard hospital

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Partnering with voluntary organizations is one of the smartest ways to bring care straight to underserved communities.

question: How must controlled substances be stored on a hospital ward?

options.A: In an open metal tray on the main nurses' station desk
options.B: Inside the patient's bedside locker for easy access
options.C: In a double-locked secure cabinet with restricted key access
options.D: Inside the general refrigerator with food items

explanation: Double-locking prevents theft, diversion, and unauthorized access to dangerous drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h6)

question: When doing nursing research, what are the three main levels used to group literature sources?

options.A: Primary, secondary, and tertiary sources
options.B: Published, unpublished, and grey sources
options.C: Clinical, historical, and theoretical sources
options.D: Qualitative, quantitative, and mixed sources

explanation: You've got this! We group literature into three tiers based on how close the information is to the original study. Primary, secondary, and tertiary keep our research organized.

question: Why is relying solely on clinical tradition dangerous in modern healthcare?

options.A: Patients always reject care based on historical habits
options.B: Traditions are often outdated and unsupported by current evidence
options.C: Traditions cost too much money to maintain in hospitals
options.D: Physicians refuse to follow traditional nursing methods

explanation: Habits passed down through generations of staff may be ineffective or even harmful compared to modern tested methods. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which food item is best suited for adding hidden calories to a bowl of porridge?

options.A: Sliced green cucumber
options.B: Clear vegetable broth
options.C: Diet lemon water
options.D: Peanut butter

explanation: Peanut butter is rich in both healthy fats and proteins, providing a dense boost of calories when stirred into soft foods. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h4)

question: When would you choose an intramuscular injection instead of giving pills by mouth?

options.A: When the patient cannot take oral medications
options.B: When the patient wants to avoid any skin punctures
options.C: When the medication needs to work over a full week
options.D: When the drug is completely harmless to the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is vomiting or unable to swallow, going through the muscle is a safe and reliable backup plan. Keep up the good work!

question: Which family planning method helps protect against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Latex condoms
options.D: Progestin-only pills

explanation: Condoms act as a physical barrier that blocks both sperm and infectious agents. Simple and effective!

question: What happens to a drug revolving fund over time if free drugs are given out but never paid for by a subsidy?

options.A: The pharmacy inventory will steadily deplete and collapse
options.B: The government will automatically double its funding
options.C: The fund will grow larger and more profitable
options.D: Drug manufacturers will begin supplying free items forever

explanation: Remember, a revolving fund depends on money returning when drugs are sold. If stock is given away without a replacement fund, the pharmacy will soon run out of cash to restock.

question: What is the primary purpose of plotting a partograph during labor in a rural clinic?

options.A: To measure the exact birth weight of the newborn infant
options.B: To record the baby's future immunization appointments
options.C: To monitor the progress of labor and detect deviations early
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used to track cervical dilation and fetal condition, helping midwives spot prolonged labor promptly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical practice when presenting qualitative research results?

options.A: Revealing the real names of participants to give them credit
options.B: Reporting all findings honestly, even unexpected ones
options.C: Separating factual results from personal opinions
options.D: Using pseudonyms to protect participant confidentiality

explanation: Participant confidentiality is paramount; revealing real names without explicit consent breaches ethical research standards. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a point source of water pollution?

options.A: Pesticides washing off multiple farms after a storm
options.B: General urban stormwater runoff from neighborhood streets
options.C: A factory discharge pipe leading directly into a river
options.D: Rainwater washing oil off a busy city highway

explanation: Correct! A point source has one clear, easy-to-spot origin, like a specific factory pipe or waste outlet.

question: Why is embedding midwives within local Nigerian communities so effective for maternal health?

options.A: It ensures that mothers never experience any pregnancy complications.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for primary health care centers.
options.C: It builds trust and helps overcome cultural and geographical barriers.
options.D: It allows midwives to practice without any formal government oversight.

explanation: When midwives live and work within the community, they break down distance and trust barriers that usually discourage women from seeking care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why do you hold the first removed glove inside the palm of your remaining gloved hand?

options.A: To stop the latex from releasing powder into the air
options.B: To easily peel off the second glove without touching its dirty outside
options.C: To keep the first glove clean so you can use it again
options.D: To save space in the waste bin

explanation: Ball up the first glove in your palm so your bare fingers can safely slide under the clean inner cuff of the second glove. Clever and safe!

question: What is the primary public health goal of proper food storage?

options.A: To reduce the cost of grocery bills
options.B: To improve the taste of meals
options.C: To make cooking faster every day
options.D: To prevent foodborne illnesses

explanation: Keeping food properly stops harmful bacteria and germs from multiplying, which directly protects people from getting sick. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h1)

question: Which clinical sign is a classic indicator of acute bilirubin entering the brain in a newborn?

options.A: Having an abnormally fast breathing rate with chest indrawing
options.B: Passing frequent watery green stools during feeding times
options.C: Developing a sudden red rash across the chest and abdomen
options.D: Arching the back and neck backward into an opisthotonos position

explanation: Opisthotonos (severe backward arching of the body) is a classic warning sign that bilirubin is irritating the baby's central nervous system. You're building expert clinical instincts!

question: Who is considered a 'susceptible host'?

options.A: A patient who has complete immunity against all infections
options.B: An individual whose immune system cannot resist an invading pathogen
options.C: A person who currently carries a germ without symptoms
options.D: An object or surface where bacteria live and multiply

explanation: Right on! A susceptible host is simply someone whose body defense is low enough for germs to easily move in and cause sickness.

question: What is the primary purpose of giving intravenous fluids in Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: To raise blood pressure to normal levels
options.B: To shrink the size of the primary tumor
options.C: To flush out uric acid and protect the kidneys
options.D: To replace lost red blood cells

explanation: Aggressive hydration forces urine production, helping the kidneys wash away dangerous breakdown products like uric acid and potassium. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which diagnostic test is best when checking for a suspected amoebic liver abscess?

options.A: Liver ultrasound or CT scan
options.B: A simple routine chest x-ray
options.C: Urine dipstick analysis
options.D: Barium swallow fluoroscopy

explanation: Correct! Imaging like an ultrasound gives a clear view of the liver to spot any fluid or abscesses.

question: An antenatal patient complains that her iron pills make her stool dark and cause mild constipation. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Instruct her to stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills
options.B: Explain that dark stools are harmless and suggest increasing fluid and fiber intake
options.C: Tell her to double the dose so her body adjusts faster to the iron
options.D: Refer her urgently to the surgeon for a bowel obstruction evaluation

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Dark stools are completely normal with iron supplements. Reassuring the patient and encouraging water and local vegetables/fiber helps her stick to her treatment without fear.

question: Why is it a bad idea to use straight, unconditioned ice packs when packing a vaccine carrier?

options.A: It creates an unpleasant smell inside the carrier
options.B: It prevents the lid from closing tightly
options.C: It can freeze and ruin sensitive vaccines
options.D: It will melt too fast and flood the container

explanation: Unconditioned ice packs are bone-chillingly cold and can instantly freeze your vaccines on contact. Always let them sweat or 'condition' a bit first!

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle habit for supporting male reproductive health?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes regularly to stimulate circulation
options.B: Engaging in regular physical exercise routines
options.C: Limiting excessive alcohol consumption
options.D: Maintaining a healthy body weight through balanced diet

explanation: You nailed it! Smoking actually harms your blood vessels, ruining the good circulation needed for proper reproductive health.

question: How does epidemiology differ from everyday bedside nursing care?

options.A: Epidemiology treats the entire community as the patient rather than focusing on a single individual.
options.B: Epidemiology relies solely on laboratory microscope findings instead of patient interviews.
options.C: Epidemiology ignores prevention entirely to focus only on end-stage disease management.
options.D: Epidemiology only deals with surgical complications rather than chronic illnesses.

explanation: Think of it this way: bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, while epidemiology steps back to look at whole communities and find health patterns. Both are super important!

question: What key tip should you give a patient who just got a 7-day course of oral antibiotics?

options.A: Share extra pills with family members who catch the same illness
options.B: Finish all 7 days of medicine even if you feel completely better
options.C: Double the next dose if you forget to take one on time
options.D: Stop taking the capsules as soon as your fever goes away

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Feeling better doesn't mean the germs are all gone. Finish the full 7 days to wipe them out completely.

question: What type of information belongs in a standard incident report?

options.A: Derogatory remarks about an uncooperative patient
options.B: Personal opinions on which doctor or nurse caused the problem
options.C: Detailed theories on how much money the hospital might lose
options.D: Objective facts about what happened and actions taken

explanation: Correct! Incident reports need pure, unbiased facts—just the plain truth of what happened and what care was given right away.

question: A patient is shaking and sweating, but the meter reads 120 mg/dL. What is your best next step?

options.A: Assume the meter is right and ignore the symptoms
options.B: Repeat the test or consider a lab check
options.C: Leave the patient to rest
options.D: Give rapid-acting insulin

explanation: Always trust your clinical instincts! If the patient's symptoms don't match the number, recheck to be certain.

question: In statistics, what is another helpful name for an ogive graph?

options.A: Simple bar chart
options.B: Standard scatter plot
options.C: Cumulative frequency polygon
options.D: Normal frequency histogram

explanation: You got this! An ogive is just a special name for a cumulative frequency polygon because we build it by plotting running totals.

question: Which activity must occur before an HIV test is administered to a client?

options.A: Pre-test counselling
options.B: Public community notification
options.C: Mandatory partner isolation
options.D: Immediate antiretroviral drug loading

explanation: Pre-test counselling prepares the client mentally and ensures they understand the testing process and their rights. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h2)

question: Why do fertility specialists always insist on evaluating both partners during a fertility workup?

options.A: Because female infertility is extremely rare compared to male causes
options.B: To prove insurance coverage before starting expensive procedures
options.C: To rule out genetic disorders in unrelated family members
options.D: Because male and female factors contribute almost equally to infertility

explanation: That's right! Fertility struggles happen pretty evenly across both partners, so testing both saves time and heartache. Brilliant thinking!

question: What is endometriosis?

options.A: A malignant tumor originating in the cervix
options.B: The growth of endometrial tissue outside the uterus
options.C: A benign infection of the vaginal wall flora
options.D: The complete absence of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Endometriosis happens when tissue similar to the lining inside the uterus grows outside of it, causing pain. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Drinking adequate water
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Eating fresh fruits daily

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes damage blood vessels and nerves over time, making it a major physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h3)

question: Why does missing ovulation while having ongoing oestrogen exposure put the uterine lining at risk?

options.A: Without progesterone to balance it, oestrogen causes the uterine lining to overgrow
options.B: The ovaries stop producing all hormones, causing the uterus to shrink rapidly
options.C: Lack of ovulation permanently closes the cervical opening against fluids
options.D: Anovulatory cycles force toxic blood to back up into the abdominal cavity

explanation: Think of progesterone as the brake pedal for oestrogen. Without it, the uterine lining keeps building up without shedding properly.

question: Why should researchers be honest about study limitations in their published papers?

options.A: To trick reviewers into approving weak methodologies
options.B: To avoid paying taxes on research grants
options.C: To make the paper shorter and easier to read
options.D: To ensure readers interpret findings with appropriate caution

explanation: You nailed it! Total honesty about what a study *couldn't* do stops clinicians from misapplying the results on the wards.

question: Which vitamin is most easily destroyed by high-heat methods like canning?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Vitamin C is quite fragile when exposed to heat, meaning high-temperature cooking and canning can easily break it down.

question: When is the right time to chart an injection you just gave your patient?

options.A: Only if the patient reports an adverse reaction
options.B: At the end of the 8-hour shift
options.C: Before drawing the drug from the vial
options.D: Immediately after giving the injection

explanation: Always document right away! Doing it immediately keeps your records accurate and lets the rest of the healthcare team know the patient's exact medication status.

question: Which body regulates nursing and midwifery practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Pharmacists Council of National Health
options.C: Medical and Dental Consultants Association
options.D: National Union of Allied Health Workers

explanation: That's right! The NMCN sets the standards for our training and practice across the country.

question: A patient asks which eating pattern is best for keeping their blood pressure in check. What should you tell them?

options.A: A high-protein, zero-fiber carnivore diet to preserve muscle mass
options.B: A clear liquid diet to cleanse the digestive and circulatory systems
options.C: A strict low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet with high saturated fats
options.D: The DASH diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy

explanation: The DASH diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is a classic winner! It packs in potassium, calcium, and fiber from whole foods to naturally bring pressure down.

question: Why must a pregnant woman report blurred vision and a terrible headache immediately?

options.A: They mean the mother needs stronger reading glasses
options.B: They are common signs of normal hormonal adjustment
options.C: They show that the baby is moving too much inside
options.D: They indicate severe high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia

explanation: Headaches and changes in vision are classic warning signs of dangerously high blood pressure. Catching pre-eclampsia early saves lives!

question: Why does supine hypotension happen when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

options.A: Heart rate drops dangerously low to rest the cardiac muscle
options.B: The lungs expand too much and trap excess oxygen away from the tissues
options.C: The heavy uterus presses on the major blood vessels returning blood to the heart
options.D: Progesterone instantly widens all peripheral blood vessels in the upper body

question: A patient at 28 weeks reports sharp, regular tummy pains and a watery vaginal discharge. What should you suspect?

options.C: Preterm labor or rupture of membranes

question: Which counseling approach works best when you want to help a teenager change their eating habits?

question: In males, which organ sits right below the bladder and wraps around the urethra?

question: How does poor lighting contribute to home accidents?

question: Why is Family Life Education an important part of primary health care?

options.A: It eliminates all infectious diseases from the community

question: How would you describe a direct cost in patient care?

question: When we talk about extracellular fluid (ECF) outside our cells, what are its two main parts?

question: A patient on a long-term central nervous system depressant asks if they can have a glass of wine with dinner. What should you say?

options.A: Drinking one small glass of wine will help the medication absorb faster into your bloodstream

question: Why is early physical therapy encouraged soon after amputation surgery?

options.A: To stretch the skin until it breaks open for drainage
options.B: To force the brain to stop feeling the missing limb

question: What do we call a community diagnosis that zeroes in on one specific health issue or vulnerable group?

options.A: Randomized clinical diagnosis
options.B: Comprehensive community diagnosis

options.D: Problem-oriented community diagnosis

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand healthcare laws?

options.A: To avoid personal liability and protect patient rights in clinical settings
options.B: To replace hospital lawyers during lawsuits

options.D: To bypass getting consent from family members in emergencies

question: A newly diagnosed patient wants to start ARVs right away, but tests show they have active meningitis. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Switch the patient to herbal remedies instead of modern drugs
options.B: Refuse to give any counseling because the patient is too sick
options.C: Start the medication immediately without waiting for any other tests
options.D: Support delaying ART briefly while the acute meningitis is treated

explanation: Correct! For serious infections like meningitis, doctors treat the acute infection first before starting ART to prevent dangerous inflammation reactions in the immune system.

question: What is the typical length range of a normal adult fallopian tube?

options.A: 5 to 7 centimeters

question: Why are accurate health records so important in busy primary health care clinics?

options.A: They ensure continuity of care when different health workers see the same patient over time.
options.B: They are used to calculate monthly staff salaries.
options.C: They replace physical exams when the clinic is crowded.
options.D: They guarantee the clinic gets international donor funds.

explanation: Patients often see different nurses on different days. Good records ensure the next nurse knows exactly what treatment was given, keeping the patient safe and cared for smoothly!

question: What is the best way for a nurse to communicate when talking with a teenager client?

options.A: Speak loudly and use complex Latin terms
options.B: Use simple language without complicated medical jargon
options.C: Write everything down without speaking directly
options.D: Ask parents to answer all questions on behalf of the youth

question: A patient was just extubated 20 minutes ago and now has a high-pitched whistling sound when breathing in. What is the most likely cause?

question: What is the most critical absolute contraindication for a standard barium swallow test?

options.C: They cause severe spikes in systemic blood pressure
options.D: Trapping toxins inside the bowel can worsen the illness

question: How many hours should a patient normally fast before doing a barium meal test?

question: A patient is shy about discussing vaginal dryness. What is the best first thing for a nurse to do?

question: What is the main difference between an 'adolescent' and 'adolescence'?

question: Why are informal sector workers in developing regions often at a higher risk for occupational lung disease?

question: A patient taking Zidovudine feels extremely weak and dizzy. Which test should the nurse check first?

question: How does simple handwashing with soap directly help prevent illness in a community?

question: When is relying on an 'authority figure' most risky in clinical practice?

question: Why must we strictly isolate confirmed patients during a viral hemorrhagic fever outbreak?

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in nursing?

question: Why do many teenage girls experience irregular periods shortly after starting menstruation?

question: What does having an 'ability-focused mindset' mean for the healthcare team?

question: When does a medication error cross the line from a civil mistake into criminal liability?

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

question: Why must nurses avoid using stigmatizing language when talking about substance use?

question: Why is high blood pressure often called a 'silent killer'?

question: A client had a vasectomy yesterday and asks when he can go back to heavy lifting at work. What do you tell him?

question: Why are busy, noisy hospital wards poor environments for teaching patients about their medications?

options.A: Sudden weight loss
options.B: High fever and chills
options.C: Severe chest pain
options.D: No symptoms at all

explanation: Small functional cysts are usually asymptomatic and are often found incidentally during imaging tests. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h3)

question: Why is informed consent a crucial part of pre-test counselling?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from paying for laboratory reagents
options.B: It forces the patient to buy their own testing kits from the pharmacy
options.C: It guarantees that testing is completely voluntary and understood by the client
options.D: It ensures the test results will automatically be published in local newspapers

explanation: Voluntary testing respects patient autonomy and builds trust between the client and the healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h2)

question: In the common obstetric history acronym TPAL, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Pelvic diameter
options.B: Primary contractions
options.C: Preterm births
options.D: Placental position

explanation: In TPAL, P stands for preterm births—deliveries that happen before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.

question: A patient is given a medication with strong anticholinergic properties. As a nurse, what side effect should you watch out for?

options.A: Slow heart rate and heavy sweating
options.B: Constricted pupils and body tremors
options.C: Dry mouth and trouble urinating
options.D: Excessive drooling and watery diarrhea

explanation: Anticholinergic drugs shut down parasympathetic effects, leading to classic signs like a dry mouth, blurry vision, and urinary retention. You are well on your way to acing your exams!

question: What percentage of nephrons in the human kidney are classified as cortical nephrons?

options.A: About 50 percent
options.B: About 99 percent
options.C: About 85 percent
options.D: About 15 percent

explanation: The vast majority of nephrons in a healthy human kidney are cortical nephrons located mostly in the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which joint is most famously affected during a first-time gout attack?

options.A: The acromioclavicular joint of the shoulder
options.B: The proximal interphalangeal joint of the index finger
options.C: The metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe
options.D: The temporomandibular joint of the jaw

explanation: Classic nursing knowledge! The big toe joint (known clinically as the metatarsophalangeal joint) is the absolute favorite spot for a first gout flare.

question: Why do we encourage skin-to-skin contact right after a normal delivery?

options.A: It completely prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum bleeding
options.B: It speeds up the surgical healing of an episiotomy wound
options.C: It acts as a permanent immunization against childhood illnesses
options.D: It helps regulate the newborn's body temperature and encourages breastfeeding

explanation: That's right! Mum's body heat keeps the baby warm, and it gets breastfeeding off to a great start.

question: A nurse and a social worker disagree on how to discharge an elderly patient who lives alone. What should guide their next step?

options.A: Following the nurse's plan because nurses spend more time at the bedside
options.B: Letting the patient leave without any support services
options.C: Focusing on the patient's needs through shared decision-making
options.D: Escalating the disagreement to the hospital director immediately

explanation: Exactly! When team members see things differently, putting the patient's welfare first and talking it through always points the way forward.

question: A massive passenger train crash is classified under which type of disaster?

options.A: Technological Industrial Leaks
options.B: Transportation Disasters
options.C: Biological Contaminations
options.D: Natural Weather Anomalies

explanation: You got it! Accidents involving mass transport like trains, planes, and large buses are grouped as transportation disasters.

question: What makes an abortion 'unsafe' according to public health standards?

options.A: A termination done without proper surgical tools or skilled personnel
options.B: Any abortion performed after the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: Any pregnancy loss that occurs naturally without human intervention
options.D: A medical termination using only prescription oral medications

explanation: Spot on! Unsafe abortions happen when procedures are done by untrained hands or in bad conditions, putting mothers at huge risk of injury. You've got this!

question: What is an early sign of fluid overload to watch out for during rehydration therapy?

options.A: Rapid disappearance of skin pinch elasticity
options.B: Puffy eyelids and swelling around the eyes
options.C: Extreme thirst and dry cracked lips
options.D: Sunken fontanelles in infants

explanation: Puffy eyes (periorbital edema) are a classic early warning that extra fluid and sodium are starting to build up in the body's tissues.

question: Why is keeping our core body temperature within a steady, normal range so important?

options.A: To keep the skeletal muscles from contracting too quickly
options.B: To prevent the bones from becoming brittle over time
options.C: To support normal metabolic processes and cellular function
options.D: To ensure the digestive system absorbs enough water

explanation: Spot on! Our body's chemical reactions and tiny cellular engines need a stable temperature to run smoothly without breaking down.

question: What is the primary reason FGM continues to be practiced in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Deeply rooted cultural traditions and beliefs
options.B: Recommendations from international health bodies
options.C: Medical advice given by local physicians
options.D: Treatment for chronic reproductive infections

explanation: FGM persists largely because of long-standing cultural traditions, myths about purity, and social pressure rather than medical necessity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h1)

question: You want to prove your ICU needs more staff than a general ward. Which tool is best to use?

options.A: Patient dietary satisfaction surveys
options.B: Monthly facility utility bills
options.C: General hospital depreciation schedules
options.D: Patient classification system workload data

explanation: Workload data gives you the hard proof of how intense the care demands are in high-acuity areas like the ICU.

question: Why are congregate living settings like nursing homes particularly vulnerable to disease outbreaks?

options.A: The complete absence of handwashing sinks
options.B: The high rate of sudden resident discharges
options.C: The requirement for outdoor recreational sports
options.D: The close proximity of medically frail residents

explanation: Correct! When vulnerable people live close together, germs can spread fast unless we are super strict with our infection control.

question: What is a major risk if a woman hyperventilates too severely during the second stage of labour?

options.A: Rapid increase in the maternal residual lung volume
options.B: Sudden and permanent closure of the maternal airway
options.C: Complete cessation of all uterine contractions
options.D: Reduced blood flow and oxygen delivery to the placenta

explanation: Blowing off too much CO2 constricts blood vessels, which can lower the oxygen flowing to the baby. Coaching mum to breathe calmly prevents this!

question: How do traditional gender expectations usually shape how teenagers behave?

options.A: By dictating how teens act, dress, and relate to others based on societal norms
options.B: By eliminating peer pressure during early adolescence
options.C: By ensuring all teenagers develop identical psychological coping mechanisms
options.D: By removing all biological differences between males and females

explanation: Exactly! Society often hands young people a script on how to dress, talk, and act depending on whether they are male or female.

question: If a vaccine gets ruined by heat, can it be saved by putting it back in the fridge?

options.A: Yes, within twenty-four hours
options.B: Yes, if shaken thoroughly
options.C: No, potency loss is permanent
options.D: Only if it is a viral vaccine

explanation: Once heat damages a vaccine's structure, you can't reverse it. It's always better to discard spoiled doses safely than give an ineffective shot.

question: A patient scheduled for a CT scan with contrast says they have a severe allergy to shellfish. What should you do first?

options.A: Proceed with the scan because shellfish has no link to dye
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink extra water for one hour
options.C: Administer an oral dose of calcium supplements right away
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately before the test

explanation: Shellfish allergies often overlap with iodine-based contrast allergies. Always alert the doctor right away so they can order premedication or choose a safer option.

question: Which of the following conditions would NOT be considered a factor that impairs placental exchange efficiency?

options.A: Thickening of the placental membrane from infection
options.B: Maternal cigarette smoking
options.C: Increased maternal hydration and rest
options.D: Placental infarction

explanation: Normal rest and adequate hydration generally support good circulation, whereas infarctions, smoking, and infections actively damage placental exchange capacity. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h8)

question: What is the most important assessment to do before giving a patient an anti-spasmodic drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's grip strength in both hands
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the patient's neck
options.C: Checking the patient's visual acuity using a reading chart
options.D: Evaluating bowel sounds and the nature of abdominal pain

explanation: You always want to know what their pain and tummy sounds are like *before* giving the drug so you can tell if it's safe and if it actually helps them.

question: Why is it a bad idea to use young family members as language interpreters?

options.A: Hospital policies fine families for using child translators
options.B: It can lead to translation errors and breach patient privacy
options.C: Children refuse to speak during home health visits
options.D: Children are always better at medical terminology than adults

explanation: Medical terms are tough to translate, and it puts an unfair emotional burden on a child to handle sensitive health matters for their relative.

question: You notice three patients on your ward develop the same severe stomach bug within 24 hours. What should you do first?

options.A: Report the cluster to infection control and public health authorities
options.B: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to all patients on the ward
options.C: Discharge all unaffected patients immediately to clear the ward
options.D: Wait another week to see if more patients develop the same symptoms

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Quick reporting helps infection control teams step in and stop an outbreak before it grows.

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

options.A: By importing vaccines directly from international manufacturers
options.B: By taking over clinical duties and injecting vaccines themselves
options.C: By replacing the cold chain refrigerators with local coolers
options.D: By building trust and addressing local rumors or hesitancy

explanation: Local chiefs and religious leaders have powerful voices. When they support immunization, community members feel much more confident bringing their babies in.

question: Why must researchers clean their data before presenting the results?

options.A: To convert all qualitative words into numbers
options.B: To ensure the study meets word count requirements
options.C: To prevent errors from distorting the final findings
options.D: To make the statistical analysis completely unnecessary

explanation: Checking for missing values and errors beforehand ensures that the data presentation reflects true clinical realities rather than mistakes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a problem caused by severe maternal anaemia for the unborn baby?

options.A: Fetal hypoxia and distress
options.B: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.C: Preterm birth and low birth weight
options.D: Macrosomia and high birth weight

explanation: You got it! Anaemia starves the baby of oxygen and nutrients, leading to low birth weight or growth restriction—never a giant baby (macrosomia).

question: Why do hospitals rely on redundancy (like independent double-checks) for high-alert drugs like insulin?

options.A: To slow down medication administration so nurses take more break time
options.B: To have multiple independent checks catch a mistake before it reaches the patient
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department always has excess stock on hand
options.D: To increase the paperwork burden and track staff productivity

explanation: Exactly! Redundancy adds a safety net. If one person has a momentary slip, the second independent check is there to catch it.

question: What does a Timed Up and Go (TUG) test primarily evaluate?

options.A: Mobility, balance, and fall risk
options.B: Lung capacity and breathing rate
options.C: Cardiovascular endurance during rest
options.D: Upper body strength and grip

explanation: The TUG test observes a patient rising from a chair, walking a short distance, and returning, which directly measures functional mobility and balance. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which enzyme do thioamide medications block to stop the thyroid from making too many hormones?

options.A: Cyclooxygenase-2
options.B: Thyroid peroxidase
options.C: Angiotensin-converting enzyme
options.D: Pancreatic amylase

explanation: Thioamides target thyroid peroxidase, which is the key enzyme the gland needs to build new hormones.

question: What is the very first thing a health worker must do during community entry?

options.A: Immunize all children under five years old
options.B: Build a modern primary health care clinic
options.C: Conduct a random drug trial in the village
options.D: Gain permission from traditional rulers and gatekeepers

explanation: Respecting local leadership through formal entry and greeting gatekeepers builds trust and opens doors for the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the difference between vulnerability and capacity in a disaster setting?

options.A: Vulnerability is an administrative hospital term, while capacity is an emergency field nursing term
options.B: Vulnerability describes weaknesses that make people susceptible to harm, while capacity describes resources available to manage risk
options.C: Vulnerability refers exclusively to financial debt, while capacity refers strictly to building structures
options.D: Vulnerability is measured only after a disaster, while capacity is measured before any hazard appears

explanation: Vulnerability means what makes us prone to suffering (like weak buildings or lack of shelter), while capacity is our strength and resources to fight back!

question: When a nurse looks at an established hospital policy, what legal benchmark does it help define?

options.A: The standard of care expected of a prudent nurse
options.B: The total number of hours a nurse must sleep
options.C: The exact salary scale for different nursing ranks
options.D: The personal liability insurance cost per year

explanation: Courts look at hospital policies to figure out what a reasonably careful, well-trained nurse would have done in that exact clinical situation.

question: What does a bulging anterior fontanelle typically indicate during a physical assessment of a newborn?

options.A: Increased intracranial pressure
options.B: Low blood sugar levels
options.C: Normal developmental growth
options.D: Mild systemic dehydration

explanation: A tight, bulging soft spot on a baby's head is a warning sign that pressure inside the skull is higher than normal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h3)

question: What is widely considered the gold standard of psychological treatment for ICT addiction?

options.A: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy
options.B: Strict physical punishment
options.C: Electroconvulsive therapy
options.D: Total isolation from society

explanation: CBT (the approach behind this app!) helps patients spot unhelpful thought patterns and build practical coping skills to manage their screen habits.

question: What does a rising serum lactate level usually mean for a sick patient?

options.A: Red blood cells are multiplying too quickly in the bone marrow
options.B: The patient is eating too many carbohydrates in their tube feeding
options.C: The kidneys are filtering waste products much faster than normal
options.D: Tissues are not getting enough oxygen and are using anaerobic metabolism

explanation: When cells are starved of oxygen, they switch to an emergency backup energy system that leaves behind lactic acid as waste. High lactate = cells need oxygen!

question: Why is earning a small income inside a sheltered workshop important for clients?

options.A: It pays for all their long-term housing and medical care
options.B: It boosts personal dignity and reduces total financial dependence
options.C: It allows them to completely stop taking prescribed medications
options.D: It guarantees promotion to a corporate manager position

explanation: Making even a modest amount of money helps clients feel valued, proud, and less like a financial burden on their families. You're learning fast!

question: What do biochemical tests mainly measure to help identify an unknown bacterium?

options.A: The patient's immune antibody response to the infection
options.B: The exact physical length and width of the cell wall
options.C: The specific chemical and metabolic activities of the organism
options.D: The genetic sequence of the organism's outer capsule

explanation: Spot on! These tests check what foods the bacteria can eat or what waste products they make, revealing their identity.

question: How do health ministries primarily use vital statistics data?

options.A: To test the speed of computer networks in wards
options.B: To decide which medications taste best
options.C: To allocate medical budgets and place facilities
options.D: To grade nursing students on final exams

explanation: Governments use population data to figure out where to spend money and build clinics based on real community needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: A patient asks why eating soluble fiber helps protect their heart. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Fiber burns off extra calories before they turn into body fat
options.B: Fiber binds to cholesterol in your digestive tract so your body removes it
options.C: Fiber directly opens up tight blood vessels to improve circulation
options.D: Fiber replaces all the salt in your meals so your kidneys can rest

explanation: Soluble fiber binds with cholesterol-containing bile acids in the intestine, preventing their reabsorption and promoting their excretion in stool. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: What is the main difference between a study conclusion and a recommendation?

options.A: Conclusions are optional, while recommendations are mandatory for all papers
options.B: Conclusions use statistics, while recommendations use personal opinions
options.C: Conclusions summarize main findings, while recommendations suggest future actions
options.D: Conclusions appear in the introduction, while recommendations are in the abstract

explanation: A conclusion wraps up what you found out, while a recommendation suggests what should be done next in practice.

question: Why does kidney compensation take longer than lung compensation during an acid-base imbalance?

options.A: Kidneys must slowly adjust tubular secretion and bicarbonate synthesis over days
options.B: Renal blood flow is too slow to deliver chemical messages effectively
options.C: Kidneys only operate when the patient is asleep and resting
options.D: Metabolic acids take longer to dissolve in plasma than dissolved gases

explanation: The lungs can change your breathing rate in seconds, but the kidneys need hours to days to manufacture new bicarbonate and adjust what they filter out.
